newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian shares' thin trade scares some to sell.
newsitem.headline: Russian shares' thin trade scares some to sell.

text.p: Leading Russian shares recovered some early morning losses on Wednesday after a nervous sell-off by operators spooked by the thinly-traded market, traders said.
Many predicted the market would correct gently for at least a week, consolidating a month-long 30 percent gain and facing a usual summer lull.
The RTS index at 0900 GMT had fallen about two percent from Tuesday's close to 460.44 on $20 million market volume.

Market leader national power utility UES EESR.RTS had firmed to $0.3975 at 0955 GMT from a morning low of $0.3910 and $0.4100 at the previous close. Rostelekom RTKM.RTS ticked up to $4.27 from a low of $4.15 and $4.18 on Tuesday.
Oil producer LUKoil LKOH.RTS had traded up to $20.65 from $20.25 and $21.05 on Tuesday.
"The morning fall was linked to some pessimism on emerging markets," said United City Bank trader Samit Yakovlev, who predicted the market would ease for a month or more.
"Many were scared by the absence of buyers over the last few days, so some tried to sell. But now the situation has improved with a few buyers appearing."

Regent European Securities trader Alexander Fonarkov said ADR selling overnight in New York had pushed down prices and that Russian economic indicators showing the economy was still shrinking had been a weak, negative force on prices.
He said that some second-tier shares which had seen buyers looking for value recently were being sold.
